## What

Shorten the required gate by removing its duplicate integration run, parallelizing repository journeys with explicit shared-resource groups, and overlapping end-to-end and unit tests on Linux and macOS. Final measured gates take 22–31 minutes on Linux/macOS and 70–72 minutes on Windows; required checks, coverage floors and the release pull request’s full sweep remain intact.

## Why

Pull requests waited one to two hours for their slowest gate, exceeding the publication path’s one-hour check wait and leaving finished work unmerged. Reducing that wait frees runner capacity and lets subsequent changes proceed sooner.

## Additional info

### Measurements

Recorded job and step durations come from `gh run view <id> --json jobs`; task timings come from the gate logs’ pytest and nextest summaries. No workflow was re-run, cancelled or dispatched.

| Run | Commit | Configuration |
|---|---|---|
| [main: 38129622038](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38129622038) | 49e7cd1 | Baseline full sweep |
| [A: 38151133403](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38151133403) | f6da20b | Remove duplicate integration run; trial reduced Rust coverage |
| [B: 38159308802](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38159308802) | 79559e5 | Add xdist |
| [C: 38165363260](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38165363260) | c15498e | Restore Rust coverage; overlap tiers on every platform |
| [D: 38172314896](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38172314896) | 6f42c33 | Disable overlap on Windows; group release drafting journeys |
| [E: 38181620797](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38181620797) | c3d425a | Reserve one Windows processor for the host; merge #189 |
| [F: 38188847711](https://github.com/nickderobertis/printobserver/actions/runs/38188847711) | 30218a6 | Final tree: OctoPrint lifecycle journey follows the parallel session |

Gate job durations in minutes; ✗ denotes time to failure, not a completed gate.

| Run | linux-x86_64 | linux-aarch64 | macos-aarch64 | windows-x86_64 | windows-aarch64 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| main | 58.8 | 51.0 | 89.9 | 137.5 | 124.5 |
| A | 33.2 | 29.2 | 65.3 | 106.9 | 88.2 |
| B | 25.6 | 19.7 | 42.8 | 85.7 | 68.0 |
| C | 21.7 | 16.3 ✗ | 29.4 ✗ | 79.9 | 83.9 ✗ |
| D | 26.4 | 20.1 | 31.2 | 132.2 | 86.5 ✗ |
| E | 19.0 | 18.7 | 31.6 | 103.1 | 85.1 ✗ |
| **F** | **30.6** | **21.8** | **27.4** | **70.2** | **71.7** |

Runner variation limits attribution from individual comparisons. Windows x86’s sequential test tier took 39.7 minutes in B and 66.4 in D; `repo-checks:test` ranged from 1528 to 3879 seconds across Windows measurements. Linux x86’s final run was about 1.6× slower across tasks than E, with lint taking 5.4 rather than 2.1 minutes.

### 1. Remove the duplicate integration run

The required integration jobs retain `octoprint-up`, `test-integration` and `octoprint-down`. The gate retains the clean-copy assertions that OctoPrint is alive after bring-up and gone after bring-down, without running the integration tier again. AGENTS.md now describes that division.

| Platform | `repo-e2e` seconds, main → A | Gate minutes, main → A |
|---|---:|---:|
| linux-x86_64 | 2650.7 → 1103.4 | 58.8 → 33.2 |
| linux-aarch64 | 2385.9 → 1003.0 | 51.0 → 29.2 |
| macos-aarch64 | 4403.4 → 2275.3 | 89.9 → 65.3 |
| windows-x86_64 | 4950.9 → 3523.6 | 137.5 → 106.9 |
| windows-aarch64 | 4669.5 → 2816.9 | 124.5 → 88.2 |

This removed 23–35 minutes from the still-serial `repo-e2e` task. A also changed Rust instrumentation, measured separately below. The retained lifecycle journey took 34 seconds locally, compared with approximately 32 minutes for its predecessor.

### 2. Parallelize repository journeys

`repo-e2e` uses `pytest -n auto --dist loadgroup`, followed by the OctoPrint journey marked `alone`.

| Platform | `repo-e2e` seconds, A → B | Gate minutes, A → B | Final parallel + alone seconds, F |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| linux-x86_64 | 1103.4 → 646.0 | 33.2 → 25.6 | 1080 + 33 |
| linux-aarch64 | 1003.0 → 429.2 | 29.2 → 19.7 | 682 + 22 |
| macos-aarch64 | 2275.3 → 1184.9 | 65.3 → 42.8 | 1353 + 59 |
| windows-x86_64 | 3523.6 → 2503.4 | 106.9 → 85.7 | 1971 + 39 |
| windows-aarch64 | 2816.9 → 1755.9 | 88.2 → 68.0 | 1818 + 74 |

Measured runners had four logical processors and 15.6–16.0 GiB RAM on Linux/Windows, and three processors and 7.0 GiB on macOS. Free disk ranged from 10.4 to 98.8 GiB. Worker selection uses one worker per available processor, bounded by 2 GiB RAM per worker; Windows reserves one processor for the host from E onward. Disk is logged but does not bound workers because journeys retain their temporary directories regardless of concurrency.

Shared resources are serialized through three groups, without loosening assertions or deadlines:

- `repo-root-release-build`: `target/release`, `target/package`, `dist/` and the Windows user `Path`.
- `repo-root-debug-build`: repository-root debug builds, Docker systemd, launchd and Windows services.
- `release-plz-drafting`: rustdoc builds from `cargo-semver-checks`, whose concurrent drafting journeys exceeded their 120-second bound on Linux ARM and Windows ARM in C.

The OctoPrint journey runs after the parallel session because Windows ARM’s process-table query takes 23–24 seconds even in the integration jobs, close to its existing 30-second bound. It exceeded that bound beside other journeys in D and E; F preserves the bound and isolates the journey.

### 3. Overlap end-to-end and unit tests where measurement supports it

Off Windows, `just check` starts `test-e2e` beside the test tier and waits for both, propagating either failure. The end-to-end target waits only for `printobserver:build`. Its existing `implicitDependencies` remain necessary for affected-project selection: a probe showed that moving them solely into `dependsOn` made Nx omit `repo-e2e` from affected projects. Added journeys exercise selection for every directly exercised project, a transitive server dependency, and exclusion for the unrelated Obico environment. The edge suppression now explains this distinction.

The measured span below runs from the test tier’s start through completion of test, end-to-end and coverage work. Corresponding gate durations are in the run table above.

| Platform | B, sequential | C | D | E | F |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| linux-x86_64 | 21.6 min | 17.5 | 19.9 | 15.2 | 22.9 |
| linux-aarch64 | 16.8 min | 13.1 | 14.6 | 14.6 | 16.1 |
| macos-aarch64 | 38.0 min | 25.2 | 25.6 | 25.3 | 24.0 |

Overlap saved approximately 12–14 minutes on macOS and 1–6 minutes on Linux in the earlier comparisons; F’s slower Linux x86 runner erased that gain in its individual comparison.

Windows retains sequential tiers. In C, overlap increased `repo-checks:test` from 1916 to 3540 seconds on x86 and from 1528 to 3879 seconds on ARM; Windows ARM’s gate increased from 68.0 to 83.9 minutes before failing. Nx parallelism remains at three: xdist already supplies additional concurrency off Windows, while the Windows overlap trial demonstrated contention.

### 4. Measure Rust instrumentation and retain existing coverage

The reduced-coverage trial was reverted in `59d2551`.

| Platform | `printobserver` nextest seconds, main → A | Test tier minutes, main → A | Longest test-tier task |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| windows-x86_64 | 1662.5 → 1332.4 | 49.5 → 43.7 | `repo-checks`, 2525.0 → 2099.5 s |
| windows-aarch64 | 1959.7 → 1642.4 | 39.6 → 35.3 | `repo-checks`, 2007.6 → 1656.3 s |
| macos-aarch64 | 114.0 → 122.1 | 11.7 → 20.9 | `repo-checks` |
| linux-aarch64 | 104.3 → 99.4 | 8.0 → 9.1 | `release-artifacts` |

The trial reduced one Windows task by 16–20%, but that task did not determine the test tier’s duration; elsewhere there was no material measured benefit. Rust coverage therefore remains on every platform with readable profiles, with the existing 95% floor and Windows ARM exemption. Windows-specific code, including `windows_service.rs` and `cfg(windows)` arms, retains its existing measurement. Python and TypeScript coverage are unchanged.

### Remaining time against the 30-minute target

| Platform | Final gate, F | Difference from target |
|---|---:|---:|
| linux-x86_64 | 30.6 min | +0.6 min; C–E ranged from 19.0–26.4 |
| linux-aarch64 | 21.8 min | −8.2 min |
| macos-aarch64 | 27.4 min | −2.6 min |
| windows-x86_64 | 70.2 min | +40.2 min |
| windows-aarch64 | 71.7 min | +41.7 min |

Windows remains above target. In F, serial `repo-checks:test` took 1670–1703 seconds and `printobserver:test` took 1366–1836 seconds, almost entirely in `every_client_command_is_proven_against_a_real_supervisor`. Together they bound a roughly 34-minute test tier, followed by roughly 33 minutes of repository journeys. Follow-ups were drafted for parallelizing `repo-checks` with declared shared resources, splitting the large client-command journey, and reducing the Windows ARM process-table read.

`ci.yml` is unchanged: `pr-title`, `llmlint`, all five gate contexts and all five integration contexts remain produced on pull requests. Release branches still select the full sweep. Release configuration, dependency declarations and release-journey assertions are unchanged; those journeys only gain scheduling groups.
